msg: DESIGN TARGET, and the SHARP form of this bench's claim. Rail sensitivity measured AT the buffered pedestal node /VREF, which is the only path by which the rail reaches the output: design R3/(R2+R3) = 10.0k/131k = 0.076336 V/V, measured 0.0763352 - agreement to six digits. A wrong R2 or R3 moves this directly.

DESIGN TARGET (blocks.md B6). Same sensitivity measured end to end at J2: 0.0771 V/V. It reads about 0.0008 V/V higher than the divider ratio above, and that residue is macromodel scaffolding, not circuit - every clamp node in the gopamp model is defined as V(vp) - const and carries ngspice's default 1e-12 GMIN to a high-impedance node, so it tracks the rail very slightly. dvr_dvs is the bound to trust for the divider; this one is the loose end-to-end guard.

REQUIREMENTS Q10 + Q6. Full scale must not clip at the -5 % rail; the OPA2333 ceiling there is 3.135 - 0.03 = 3.105 V and the design lands at 3.0251 V, clearing blocks.md B6's own 3.02 V figure by 5.1 mV. That margin was only 2.1 mV while R6 = 100 R was fitted, and would have gone NEGATIVE at the 470 R that would have been needed to make an isolation resistor actually work - one of the reasons R6 was removed at P4.
REQUIREMENTS Q7 (12-bit usable over the output span). Usable span at the -5 % rail, design 2.785 V, measured 2.7847 V; 2.70 V still leaves 0.66 mV per 12-bit LSB.
DESIGN TARGET. Pedestal at the -5 % rail: 3.135*10/131 = 0.2393 V plus the static 1.15 mV common-mode term; measured 0.2404 V.
DESIGN TARGET. Pedestal at the +5 % rail: 3.465*10/131 = 0.2645 V plus the same static term; measured 0.2659 V.
